concept.name: Average execution price
concept.definition: The quantity-weighted average price at which an order's fills executed: total value traded divided by total quantity filled for that order. It is the price actually achieved across what may be many partial executions at different levels.
concept.intuition: If your 1,000 shares came in five pieces at five prices, the average execution price is the single number that correctly prices the whole position.
concept.mechanics: The venue accumulates price-times-quantity across all fills of the order chain and reports it as a running field (FIX AvgPx, tag 6) that updates with each partial fill; for multi-day good-till orders it spans all days' executions. Slippage and transaction-cost metrics are computed against this average.
concept.formula: AvgPx = sum(fill price_i x fill qty_i) / sum(fill qty_i) = CumValue / CumQty.
concept.failure_modes: Averaging hides the distribution: two orders with the same AvgPx can have very different market-impact profiles. Booking systems that mix up per-day and cumulative averages on multi-day orders produce wrong cost basis.
concept.misconceptions: Average execution price is not the market VWAP - it is weighted by your own fills only, over your order's lifetime. Nor is it necessarily the price of any single actual print.
concept.example: You buy 400 shares at $25.00 and 600 at $25.10; the average execution price is (400x25.00 + 600x25.10)/1,000 = $25.06.

citations.source: FIX 4.2 Execution Report (MsgType 8), FIX Dictionary (Onix Solutions)
